page.layout: One printed page, single column of text, with a verse epigram in italic at top, a rule, a centred heading with subtitle, then a verse poem with a drop initial. Margin notes: none legible on the printed page itself. Signature "A 5" and catchword "Trino" at the foot right.

p.i: Sic humana salus toto curabitur orbe:
Gilberto praeunte, BREVEM mox adseret ARTEM;
Et VITÆ LONGOS adseret ille COLOS.

main_text.head: ENCOMIUM ALTERUM,

p.i: Eidem viro Philosophicis scriptis claro, & nunc demum Medicinos libros feliciter molienti.

main_text.p: POstquam beatas Cœlitum petiit domos Ingens Lycei lumen Heurnius pater; Cœloque postquam clarus ille Pavius, Suadæ medulla, fidus additum novum: Nil è cathedris prodiit Galenicis. Apollinare obmutuit collegium. Non scripta cedro digna vendidit Tryphō, Coæ insulæ illa, aut invidenda Pergamo. Manus deorum desiêre pharmacum, Opemque ferre languidis mortalibus. Nemo est, ut ante, sævi ab Orci faucibus Retractus, ipse gaudet umbris Cerberus,

page.notes: The initial P of the poem is a large drop capital, joined to "Ostquam". The poem's first line is set with the drop initial; the "Trino" and "A 5" at the foot are the catchword and signature. The rule above the heading is a printed ornamental rule, not text. Some letters in the poem are slightly damaged by ink and the scan edge; readings are as best seen. Faint show-through of the facing page is present in the left margin and is not transcribed.
